status: proposal (claude-a/progression, 25 Oct); every number is a placeholder until play-tests and Claude L's harness

builds_on.abilities: game/data/abilities/<id>.json (Codex C60, PR #261, branch codex/godot-ability-kits): the base kit and the powered form are canonical and unchanged here
builds_on.game_design: docs/vision/game-design.md (PR #223): level 1 to 30 shared, perks pick 1 of 3, gear level and the forge, Glint, scrap and region materials

levels.late_joiner: arrives at the shared level with every technique and upgrade it has reached
levels.perks: unchanged from game-design.md section 6: a card of three at every level; techniques are fixed milestones on top
levels.inputs: no new buttons: every technique binds to primary, secondary, block, special, dodge, a timing window or a passive condition. None uses a hold on primary (Codex's primary repeats while held)

rules: Each folk's signature weapon is the item its kit is built on; tiers change its drawing and add one small handling change each.
No tier multiplies damage. Power comes from gear level and the forge (game-design.md 5.6 and appendix B), so a tier never becomes a second damage curve.
A tier keeps the weapon's grip and release anchors within 1 px; a longer tier records its own anchors in the manifest.
A folk who joins late arrives at the highest tier the forge has already opened, except Starfall, which is always a forge step.
weapon_tiers.starshard: a fist-sized splinter of moon; guaranteed on the first defeat of every boss from act 3 on and from the deep shards after the story; Moss's stall sells them at a fixed high price after the story. Never random-priced, never timed
weapon_tiers.smith: Hale, at the forge (game/core/village.gd restore id 'forge'); 'Show me' previews the next tier on the folk before paying

cosmetics.rule: Outfits are looks only. Accessories are looks only, except each folk's trinket, which carries one small perk marked 'proposal'. Only the active folk's trinket counts, so perks never stack.

slots.outfit: the body's cloth and colours; one at a time; 'home' is the drawn look
slots.head: a hat or headpiece; for Ashe, Brine and Rook it dresses the helmet instead (a hat cannot coexist with the helmet they wear)
slots.back: cloak, cape or what rides on the back; never hides tagged back gear (quiver, pack, slung rifle, loader frame)
slots.trinket: a small belt or chest charm, 2 to 4 px

sources.story: a quest's end: the folk's own quest (game-design 8.3) or a named main or village quest. Event quest:<id>:done; quest ids are Claude K's and are placeholders here
sources.arena: a first rank in a ring (game-design 9). Event arena:<ring>:<bronze|silver|gold>. Never Star (Hard only)
sources.village: a building restored to a tier (game-design 7.3). Event restore:<building>:<tier>
sources.bond: any familiar reaching a bond level (game-design 4.1). Event bond:any:<level>
sources.drop: a rare drop from camp chests and elites in one region (looter-lite). Event drop:<region>
sources.glint: bought at Moss's stall at a fixed price once the stall tier stocks it. Event buy:stall:<item>

drop_rules.bad_luck_counter: guaranteed by the 12th camp chest in that region
drop_rules.drops_for_folk_not_yet_met: kept in the wardrobe, shown when they join

cosmetics.ramps: names in item 'ramps' and tier 'materials' are descriptive; '(new)' marks a ramp to add to castwork palette.py with four tones (deep, shadow, base, light, optional shine); others name the material already on that part

save.status: proposal for the save owner; nothing here changes game/core/save_game.gd

fields.folk.<id>.look: {outfit, head, back, neck, trinket}: item ids or null
fields.seen: [ids] for the 'new' marks; techniques are derived from level, never stored
